name: ansilove
why: Renders old BBS ANSI art files into PNG, a satisfying look at a forgotten art form and its formats.

brief.what_it_is: AnsiLove/C is a command-line converter that turns ANSI and ASCII text-mode art files from the BBS and artscene era into PNG images. It takes files in formats such as ANS, PCB, BIN, ADF, IDF, TND and XB, reads any SAUCE metadata record, and writes a size-optimized 4-bit PNG, optionally with Retina @2x or custom scale output. The project is by Frederic Cambus, Stefan Vogt and Brian Cassidy, and the latest release listed on the homepage is 4.2.2 from June 10, 2026.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says it is a complete rewrite of the earlier AnsiLove/PHP in C, chosen for PHP interpreter independence, performance, and a reusable library. The homepage explains the origin: the author started it in 2003 to convert their own ASCII and ANSI artworks into PNG images for a demoscene gallery.
brief.how_it_works: The tool loads the input through the libansilove library, which parses the text-mode escape sequences or raw video-memory dump for the detected format and draws each character cell using embedded binary font dumps, with iCE colors and SAUCE hints where enabled. It then writes the canvas out as a PNG. The README says the renderer uses a 4-bit palette to keep files small.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the project builds from source with CMake and needs the libansilove library and its header files installed first. Binary libansilove packages exist for OpenBSD, NetBSD, FreeBSD, Debian, Ubuntu and Solus; on other systems the README says libansilove must be installed manually. The README asks for C99 with GCC or Clang. Setting ENABLE_SECCOMP=1 when invoking CMake enables experimental seccomp sandboxing on selected architectures. No accounts, runtimes or first-run configuration are mentioned.
brief.standout: It is a small, C99, BSD-licensed converter that also doubles as a SAUCE reader (-s) and a library, and it ships embedded PC and Amiga bitmap fonts so output matches original DOS and Amiga text modes. Options such as -b 9 for the 9th block column and -m ced for Amiga-style black-on-gray output reproduce real hardware look rather than a generic font.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage lists a 4.2.2 release dated June 10, 2026, with changelog entries for a Nix package link and a SAUCE font fix, preceded by a 4.2.1 release in March 2025. The README is current and lists packages across many distributions. I could not see a last-commit date from the pages I read.
brief.caveats: Experimental seccomp support is only for selected architectures. Input must be a supported format, and files with unknown suffixes default to the ANSi renderer. Font names such as cp437 and topaz500+ are case-sensitive, and the default column count is 80 except 160 for BIN. The README says the tool is tested on Linux and OpenBSD, and other compilers may work but are not tested. Some options such as -c, -b and -m are only needed occasionally, because defaults usually work. The brew formula description is simply ANSI/ASCII art to PNG converter, and the tool does not make the PNG preview of the earlier PHP web converter available.

judge.reason: It revives obscure BBS and artscene formats as faithful images, exposing text-mode graphics, hardware fonts, and metadata most developers have never encountered.

entry.title: ansilove
entry.tldr: Turns old BBS-era ANSI and ASCII art files into PNG images, using the original DOS and Amiga fonts so they look the way they did on screen.
entry.deeper_look:
ansilove reads text-mode art files from the BBS and demoscene era (ANS, PCB, BIN, ADF, IDF, TND, XB and others) and writes them out as small 4-bit PNGs. It reads the SAUCE metadata record if one is present, and it can output Retina @2x or other scales.

The interesting part is that this art was never made of pixels. A file is a stream of characters, colour codes and escape sequences, and the picture only exists once something draws each character cell with a particular font. ansilove carries embedded PC and Amiga bitmap fonts so the result matches the original text modes rather than a generic monospace look. Options like `-b 9` for the 9th block column and `-m ced` for Amiga-style black-on-gray output reproduce specific hardware quirks.

The author started the project in 2003 to convert their own ASCII and ANSI artworks into PNGs for a demoscene gallery. This C version is a rewrite of the earlier AnsiLove/PHP, chosen to drop the PHP dependency, run faster, and let the parsing and rendering live in a reusable library, libansilove. The tool is by Frederic Cambus, Stefan Vogt and Brian Cassidy.

It also works as a SAUCE reader with `-s`, which is a handy way to see who made a file, what group it came from and which font it expects.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the option summary: output file, font, column count, bit mode, scale factor and file type.
Renders an ANSI art file to out.png, using the default 80-column layout and the detected format.
Shows the SAUCE metadata record of the file instead of rendering it.

entry.whats_unique: It reproduces real DOS and Amiga text-mode rendering with embedded fonts and hardware quirks, and it is a small BSD-licensed C99 tool backed by an embeddable library.
entry.caveats: You need your own ANSI art files to feed it, and font names like cp437 and topaz500+ are case-sensitive.
